scope: Composition of retained native lock-protected standard-CAL programming and retained one-through-six-bridge Unlock/Reply Network behavior; scripted cmqttd acceptance only, with no live bridge or power-cycle claim

retained_native_evidence.finding: Literal native C-Gate direct lock-protection request uses CAL Unlock for the target parameter before STORE.

Literal native C-Gate uses the same Unlock CAL in a confirmed programming exchange; the routed SYNCNEW implementation and its retained classfile evidence establish exact Reply Network correlation for this CAL through one to six bridges.
Original receiver correlation accepts Reply Network paths through one to six bridges and rejects route, unit and CAL mismatches.
The retained CBusBaseNetwork/CBusUnit class path keeps a resolved bridged network bound to standard-CAL programming commands.

cmqttd_acceptance: Transport tests require the exact Reply Network, remote unit and parameter for the unlock challenge, then the exact parameter/tag acknowledgement and full routed readback.
Direct and neighbouring-route challenges and acknowledgements cannot complete the operation.
The routed unlock and every later STORE are sent exactly once; a lost confirmation or incomplete reply faults the shared programming generation without replay.
The service test performs a routed lock-protected PP SAVE while retaining the owned target-network session and leaving physical caches untouched.
evidence_boundaries: No physical bridge or routed unit completed a lock-protected write in this acceptance run.
The original retained lock capture covers ProgramMethod=direct; cmqttd also composes the same routed challenge for page-aware paged/NCC fields and pins it in transport tests.
OEM/GOC routed methods are covered separately by native_cgate_routed_pp_methods.json; routed C-Bus 3 Save-to-NVM is evidenced separately in native_cgate_routed_nvm_commit.json.
No successful acknowledgement is treated as proof of NVM persistence or power-cycle survival.
